children: U.S. stock indices rose on Friday and posted their best weekly gains in several months amid a revival of optimism around the AI trade.

The S&P 500 gained about 5.6%, the Nasdaq 100 jumped 6.6%, and the Dow Jones index gained 5.5% in the week ending November 27. All stock indices also ended Friday higher, with the trading day cut short for Thanksgiving.

Meanwhile, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the iShares Semiconductor ETF gained between 8% and 10% this week, with Nvidia (NVDA) supporting gains. Nvidia was the third-best performer on the Nasdaq 100 for this week, with weekly gains of about 19.6%.

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits improved to the ‘extremely bullish’ territory from ‘neutral’ for the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY); it remained ‘extremely bullish’ on the Invesco QQQ (QQQ) and ‘bearish’ on the SPDR Dow Jones ETF (DIA).

While investor sentiment around AI seemed to have improved this week, as seen in the strong gains in the Nasdaq and coinciding ETFs, risks around rising borrowing costs and the longevity of the AI trade remain in doubt.
“Until the market can get a clear sense of what’s next, we should expect continued volatility,” said Tom Essaye of The Sevens Report.
Meanwhile, Anthropic PBC (ANT) share price pushed past its $83 initial public offering price on Friday, ending its first full week of trading higher.

The stock gained about 11% from its IPO price in the holiday-shortened week ending November 27. On Friday, the stock also hit its highest intraday price since Monday, snapping a two-day run of finishes below the IPO level as wider market risk appetite improved across tech stocks after the nearly month-long Nvidia (NVDA)-led selloff.
Key Trending Stocks

According to a Financial Times report, Verizon Communications (VZ) is negotiating the acquisition of broadband provider Fidium for $6 billion, a strategic transaction aimed at broadening its network coverage and capturing a larger portion of the nationwide internet customer base.
Shares of EV giant Tesla (TSLA) rose on Friday, adding to a strong weekly performance, as the company reportedly plans to acquire Germany-based machine-tool maker EMAG.
OpenAI has countersued Apple with a California lawsuit accusing the iPhone maker of stealing trade secrets and squeezing hardware suppliers to block rival devices, the FT reported on Friday.
Palantir Technologies (PLTR) secured a defense contract reportedly worth around $300 million from Poland on Friday, amid an increasing use of AI in critical defense and military operations.

U.S. shoppers are increasingly leaning on AI tools to compare models, evaluate specifications, and weigh alternatives before visiting a retailer's website or store, according to Adobe's 2026 holiday shopping data.
